articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Major Exhibition Exploring Pictorialism Opens at Tate Modern
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is hosting a new exhibition featuring over 200 rare vintage prints that explores pictorialism, the first international art photography movement.
articles.content: Tate Modern is hosting a new exhibition focusing on pictorialism, the movement that established photography as a genuine art form. Opening to visitors on 14 October 2026, the exhibition runs until 21 February 2027. Titled Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, the event brings together over 200 rare vintage photographic prints gathered from around the world. The exhibition highlights the darkroom experiments and pictorialist practices that began in the 1880s, where photographers engaged with painting compositions, moods, and aesthetics. Visitors can examine works by figures such as Alvin Langdon Coburn, Lionel Wendt, Soichi Sunami, and Lee Sow Lim, alongside exploring analogue printing processes including platinum, bromoil, and carbro prints. A working darkroom within the exhibition space offers visitors the chance to learn printmaking using vintage and environmentally friendly techniques on certain days. An audio guide is also available for purchase on smartphones to accompany the visit.

articles.originalTitle: Foster + Partners designs pair of skyscrapers connected by garden bridges in Armenia - Dezeen
articles.title: Skyscrapers Connected by Garden Bridges Designed for Yerevan
articles.excerpt: Foster + Partners has designed a pair of skyscrapers connected by garden bridges for the World Trade Center Yerevan development.
articles.content: British studio Foster + Partners has designed a pair of skyscrapers for the World Trade Center Yerevan development in the capital of Armenia. The development features two towers connected by three enclosed bridge elements, with one housing offices and the other containing apartments and a hotel. Wrapped in glazed facades, the skyscrapers feature a concrete structural frame with steel bracing. The connecting bridges will offer landscaped terraces and shared amenities for occupants. At the base of the towers, low-lying buildings will accommodate entertainment, hospitality, and shopping spaces around a public square. According to the studio, the design aims to establish a dialogue with the country's history and culture, referencing an urban masterplan originally drafted in 1924 by architect Alexander Tamanian.

articles.originalTitle: Portraits in Philanthropy: Stefan Björkman & Kieran Long - ArtReview
articles.title: Amos Anderson Fund and Amos Rex Directors Discuss Philanthropy and Risk
articles.excerpt: Established in 1940, Finland's Amos Anderson Fund continues its long-term support for the arts alongside its contemporary art museum, Amos Rex, exploring the boundaries of philanthropic risk and international engagement.
articles.content: Established in 1940 by Finnish publisher Amos Anderson, the fund known until recently as Föreningen Konstsamfundet changed its name to the Amos Anderson Fund in 2025. The fund previously opened museums in Helsinki and Söderlångvik, before transforming its Helsinki art museum into the contemporary art venue Amos Rex in 2018. Amos Anderson Fund CEO Stefan Björkman and Amos Rex Director and CEO Kieran Long discussed the institution's ongoing mission and philanthropic model. According to Björkman, the founder created the fund as an alter ego to support the arts in a young independent nation. While the fund operates at arm's length from artistic decisions, it maintains a willingness to support calculated artistic risk and emerging practitioners. Operating within central Helsinki, Amos Rex functions as a civic space focusing on research, curatorial excellence, and international collaboration. Museum representatives noted that while private philanthropy cannot replace public institutional funding, it plays a vital role in fostering renewal, supporting younger generations through projects like the Generation exhibition, and introducing international voices to the local cultural ecosystem.

articles.originalTitle: Studio Museum Announces New Artists-in-Residence - Hyperallergic
articles.title: Studio Museum Announces New Artists-in-Residence and Prix Duchamp Winner
articles.excerpt: The Studio Museum in Harlem announced its upcoming residents, while France's Prix Duchamp was awarded to artist duo Brognon Rollin. Other developments across the arts sector include institutional appointments and major museum acquisitions.
articles.content: The Studio Museum in Harlem has announced its yearlong artists-in-residence for 2026-2027. Multidisciplinary artist Turiya Adkins, artist and curator Timothy Yanick Hunter, and photographer and filmmaker Clifford Prince King will occupy individual studio spaces in the institution's new West 125th Street building starting in November through October 2027. The residency includes professional development, material support, and a culminating group exhibition. Meanwhile, the Prix Duchamp, France's largest contemporary art award, was granted to the artist duo Brognon Rollin, formed by David Brognon and Stéphanie Rollin. The winners receive a €35,000 prize, and their work is featured in an exhibition at the Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris. Museum director Fabrice Hergott praised the practice as a tenacious statement on human vulnerability. In institutional acquisitions, the New York Public Library received a trove of 250 prints by Kiki Smith gifted by her sister Seton Smith, forming the most comprehensive collection of the artist's prints in the United States. Additionally, the Cleveland Museum of Art acquired Teresita Fernández's site-specific ceramic wall murals, while various nonprofit art organizations secured reserve fund grants ranging from $15,000 to $50,000.

articles.originalTitle: Frieze London 2026 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze London Fair Spotlights Global Exhibitions and Institutional Shifts
articles.excerpt: Recent Frieze London activities highlight new cultural districts, evolving fair focuses, and diverse artistic presentations.
articles.content: The Frieze London art week brought forth numerous exhibitions, institutional developments, and awards across the UK capital. Ahead of the emirate's inaugural fair, a new cultural district named Noma was announced near the site of the upcoming Frieze Abu Dhabi. At Frieze Masters, the representation of non-Western art and galleries from the Global South shifted notably. Meanwhile, staff strikes at Goldsmiths reached 130 days, marking the longest university strike in UK history. Okiki Akinfe won the inaugural £30,000 emerging artist prize at Frieze London, supported by the Dasha Shenkman Focus Fund. Across London, various design fairs and galleries presented exhibitions, while the art world also contended with the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, which requires galleries, museums, and auction houses to report on the sustainability of their packing materials.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris 2026 to close early amidst French unrest - ArtReview
articles.title: Art Basel Paris Closes Early Amid Student Protests and Safety Concerns
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Paris has announced an early closure, canceling its public weekend days due to safety concerns and student protests across France. Organizers confirmed the fair would conclude on Friday evening.
articles.content: Art Basel Paris will close its fair early due to safety concerns arising from student protests in France. Having opened on Wednesday for VIP cardholders, the event was originally scheduled to close on Sunday but has cancelled two of its public days, concluding on Friday evening. Fair leadership, including Vincenzo de Bellis, Karim Crippa, and Carly Murphy, noted in a letter that the decision was not taken lightly and that participant safety remained the utmost priority. Social media accounts had mobilized to target the fair directly at the Grand Palais, while demonstrators previously picketed the Louvre in solidarity with wider high school student protests across the country. In response to the unrest, organizers erected anti-ram barriers around the venue and increased security measures, requiring government identification from all visitors attending on Friday. Several galleries in Paris closed their doors or scaled back surrounding events as a precaution. Organizers have not issued any statements regarding potential refunds for public tickets or exhibitor booth costs.

articles.originalTitle: Anselm Kiefer painting too large to exhibit gets its own David Chipperfield pavilion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: German Artist Anselm Kiefer's Massive Painting Receives Dedicated Pavilion
articles.excerpt: Purchased by German industrialist Reinhold Würth in 2008, a massive Anselm Kiefer painting is now publicly accessible in a purpose-built German pavilion. Designed by architect David Chipperfield, the 140 sq. m concrete building was shaped according to the artist's specifications.
articles.content: Stored for nearly two decades, a giant Anselm Kiefer painting is finally on public view following the opening of a dedicated gallery in Germany. Industrialist Reinhold Würth purchased the 11.2m high and 7.1m wide painting directly from the artist's studio in 2008, but it proved too large for existing exhibition spaces. Consequently, the Würth Group commissioned British architect David Chipperfield in 2025 to design a standalone pavilion exclusively for the artwork. Situated in the sculpture garden at Museum Würth 2 in Künzelsau, the building opened on 13 October. Titled after a poem by Paul Celan, the artwork incorporates oil, emulsion, shellac, earth, and branches on canvas. Kiefer specified the room's proportions, doorway placement, and wall colors for the freestanding structure. Bernhard Danigel of David Chipperfield Architects Berlin noted that the architectural response focused entirely on creating a quiet space dedicated to a single work. The opening coincides with the completion of a three-year renovation at the nearby Kunsthalle Würth.

articles.originalTitle: Best of Design Miami Paris 2026 – it’s aglow with highlights - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Design Miami Paris 2026 Opens Doors for Its Fourth Edition
articles.excerpt: Design Miami Paris 2026 at L'Hôtel de Maisons brings together international collectors to showcase 140 years of global design and decorative arts.
articles.content: The fourth edition of Design Miami Paris 2026 has opened at L'Hôtel de Maisons, drawing galleries and collectors to view international design and decorative arts. The fair features outdoor displays such as Pierre Renart's moabi wood bench, which won the Best Design at Large Presentation award, and Jean Prouvé's 1944 demountable house presented by Galerie Patrick Seguin. Salon 94 Design received the Best Gallery Presentation award for juxtaposing Alberto and Diego Giacometti sculptures with furniture by Rick Owens. Italian exhibitors like Nilufar displayed vintage works alongside contemporary collectible design and Christian Pellizzari's Murano glass lighting. Scandinavian representation included Mathias Bengtsson's polished stainless steel Membrane chair, which captured the award for Best Contemporary Work. Historical highlights featured a unique living room chair designed by Frank Lloyd Wright for the Ward W Willits house, securing the award for Best Work of Historical Design. The exhibition highlights a diverse range of historical masterpieces, contemporary studio works, and collectible artists' jewelry from galleries around the world.

articles.originalTitle: Our ‘Design Directory’ 2026: The architects, studios and designers to know around the world - Monocle
articles.title: Global Design Industry and Architectural Landscape Highlighted in International Directory
articles.excerpt: Monocle magazine's new design directory compiles European architects, studios and designers who combine local craftsmanship and regional vernaculars with innovative solutions to shape global industry standards.
articles.content: The global design industry continues to expand with a new international directory celebrating the firms, studios and individuals at the top of their craft. Europe's architectural and design landscape draws upon a rich history ranging from ancient structures to modernist masterpieces, with contemporary practitioners utilizing these foundations for adaptive reuse and circular economies. In Austria, architectural practices integrate regional timber-building traditions and exacting craftsmanship, alongside civic projects like Vienna's hybrid timber market hall. Belgium's modern design scene features climate-conscious landscape architecture and mixed-use urban blocks. Czechia stands out for its adaptive reuse initiatives and community-minded civic infrastructure. Denmark maintains its leadership in functional minimalism through material-focused interiors and utilitarian objects, while Finland celebrates natural materials and human-centred design. France combines haute-couture craftsmanship with technological innovations to produce sculptural interiors, sustainable architecture and cinematic spaces. Germany's contemporary scene leads in efficient architecture and regional material usage, anchored by Berlin studios focusing on community capacity and human scale. Greece blends classical antiquity with modern regionalism across large-scale developments. Together, these international practitioners shape global standards by honouring local vernaculars.

articles.originalTitle: Johnston Marklee unveils designs for Bass Museum expansion - Dezeen
articles.title: Johnston Marklee Unveils Designs for Bass Museum Expansion in Miami
articles.excerpt: California-based architecture studio Johnston Marklee has unveiled design plans to expand the Bass Museum of Art in Miami Beach, featuring elevated galleries and courtyard spaces.
articles.content: California architecture studio Johnston Marklee has unveiled designs to expand the Bass Museum of Art in Miami Beach, USA, incorporating elevated galleries and courtyard spaces. The project extends the museum into a 22,000-square-foot area at the southwest corner of the campus, adding both indoor and outdoor areas. Renderings display two rectangular pavilion structures resting on a thin concrete plane, elevated off the ground to comply with local resiliency guidelines regarding floodwater risks. Courtyards passing underneath the structure maintain an open corner and increase public access. Founding partner Sharon Johnston noted that the project will enhance public engagement with museum programs through careful spatial planning. The upper structures feature sheer white walls, while ground-level areas underneath display textured finishes. A backlit oculus at the center will illuminate night passages leading to landscape gardens. The expansion builds upon the original 1930s art deco building designed by Russell Pancoast and a subsequent expansion by Arata Isozaki. Founding partner Mark Lee stated that the project honors the site's architectural heritage. Primary exhibition spaces will occupy the rectangular pavilions, featuring white-wall galleries, rectangular windows, and a skylight.

articles.originalTitle: Collectible Art and Design Event PAD London Makes Compelling Case for Luxury Players - WWD
articles.title: PAD London Fair Brings Together Luxury Brands and Collectors
articles.excerpt: Held in Berkeley Square, the PAD London art and design fair continues to serve as a key platform for luxury brands to connect with international collectors.
articles.content: Held every October in London's Berkeley Square, the PAD London art and design fair welcomed new participants this year, including luxury brands such as Yves Salomon and Buccellati. Fair organizers stated that the event attracted younger collectors aged 30 to 45, as well as buyers from the Middle East, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Latin America. Italian jewelry brand Buccellati showcased new designs from its Macri collections and welcomed thousands of visitors to its booth during the event. Yves Salomon Éditions, bringing its renowned ready-to-wear name into the furniture and gallery sector, presented a curated selection of historic and contemporary designs. According to UBS's global collecting report, increases in first-half sales at international auction houses continue to support the recovery in the art and design market.

articles.originalTitle: The Long Goodbye - Carrie Mae Weems - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Carrie Mae Weems Explores Migration and Water at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: Artist Carrie Mae Weems presents a new film work exploring migration stories and water-shaped identities as part of V&A East Museum's new commission.
articles.content: V&A East Museum is hosting a new film installation by artist Carrie Mae Weems focusing on the theme of migration. Prepared under the Making East London Display theme, the work examines how bodies of water shape humanity and enable transatlantic migration. The piece explores how relocated communities create new identities and artistic forms in east London and beyond. Weems notes that love stories are embedded in every migration story, touching upon those left behind and what allows a new place to feel like home. The production emphasizes that water currents and migration networks fuel global creativity while celebrating the cultural diversity of contemporary cities. Supported by the Terra Foundation for American Art, the presentation is on view in the Film Room on Level 1 of the V&A East Museum. The event is free, and the exhibition remains open until Wednesday, 11 November 2026. The work was edited collaboratively by Carrie Mae Weems, Atagun Ilhan, and Yao Xu.

articles.originalTitle: These Kitchens Changed Design History Forever—Inside the Race to Save the Last Ones Standing - Architectural Digest
articles.title: Efforts to Preserve the Frankfurt Kitchen, Modern Design's Genesis
articles.excerpt: Volunteers in Frankfurt are racing against time to salvage original Frankfurt Kitchens from 1920s housing estates, protecting a foundational milestone in modern domestic architecture.
articles.content: As original fitted kitchens in Frankfurt’s 1920s housing estates face removal during apartment renovations, volunteers from the Ernst-May-Gesellschaft work to save the cook spaces from destruction. Widely regarded as a pivotal development in modern kitchen design, the Frankfurt Kitchen was designed by architect Margarete Schütte-Lihotzky in 1926 to rationalize domestic labor and lessen women's workload. Measuring just 6.2 by 11.3 feet, every inch of the space had a purpose, featuring continuous counters, built-in cabinets, an electric stove, and labeled aluminum storage bins arranged in assembly-line fashion. For years, the Ernst-May-Gesellschaft has served as an intermediary between original apartment units and cultural institutions. To prevent the kitchens from being discarded during building renovations, volunteers meticulously dismantle surviving original elements and transport them to a warehouse in Frankfurt-Fechenheim for restoration and preservation. Experts and conservators clean and restore the salvaged components, combining parts from different kitchens to reconstruct complete models for museums and academic institutions.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Beverly Buchanan - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Beverly Buchanan Featured in Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: The Biennale Arte 2026 presentation of Beverly Buchanan's work encompasses drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks that engage with Black Southern building traditions and land ownership.
articles.content: Born in Fuquay, United States, in 1940, Beverly Buchanan earned master's degrees in parasitology and public health from Columbia University before focusing on art. After exhibiting in New York City, she relocated to the American South, living in Georgia before moving to Ann Arbor, Michigan, where she died in 2015. Her presentation in the Biennale Arte 2026 spans drawing, painting, sculpture, earthworks, and archival field notes and writings. Buchanan's shack sculptures honor Black cultural preservation, commemorating self-taught builders and artists such as Mary Lou Furcron and Nellie Mae Rowe. Utilizing reclaimed timber, metal, medical spatulas, and cement mixes including tabby—a concrete incorporating oyster shells, sand, and ash—Buchanan's material practice reflects histories of custodianship, land ownership, and coastal survival in the American South.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Issa Samb - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Features Installations Dedicated to Issa Samb
articles.excerpt: The 2026 edition of Biennale Arte presents installations inspired by the Dakar courtyard of Senegallist artist Issa Samb, highlighting his multidisciplinary practice and grassroots artistic philosophy.
articles.content: Born in Dakar in 1945 and passing away there in 2017, Senegallist artist Issa Samb is featured in the Central Pavilion and Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026. Hailing from the Lebou community of sanctuary keepers, Samb worked across painting, collage, assemblage, sculpture, performance, and writing. He co-founded the Laboratoire Agit'Art collective with filmmaker Djibril Diop Mambéty and others, championing a grassroots, autonomous approach focused on public engagement rather than conventional cultural politics. His presence at the 2026 Biennale is articulated through installations inspired by his central Dakar home and courtyard, La Cour, which historically served as a meeting place for artistic and political thought. The presentation features costumes, suspended objects, assemblages, notes, and sketches. Additionally, a video contribution by Adrienne Edwards documents a visit to La Cour, while Ican Ramageli's film Cap Vers l’Est portrays Samb exploring liminal spaces where the living meets the dead. The exhibition runs from May through November.

articles.originalTitle: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1B in Total Costs - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1B in Total Costs
articles.excerpt: The total cost of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago has reached $1 billion, more than double its original estimate, driven by expanded construction scope, public art, and insurance costs.
articles.content: The complete campus of the Barack Obama Presidential Center is now expected to cost $1 billion, more than twice its original $350-million price tag. The most recent filing from the non-profit Obama Foundation stated that the latest cost projection for the campus is about $91 million above the September figure, excluding publicly financed infrastructure improvements. Lakeside Alliance is the joint venture contractor that completed the main building on the campus earlier this year. The foundation noted that the latest increases were for additional construction scope, such as the 60,000-sq-ft Home Court basketball center, public art, and insurance. Emily Bittner, the foundation's vice president of communications, stated in an interview that they anticipate the total cost is approximately $1 billion, all raised through private contributions. The original project budget was announced as $350 million, grew to $500 million when design was completed in 2017, and reached $850 million in early September before the latest filing. The foundation stated it has no outstanding disputed charges with Lakeside Alliance.

articles.originalTitle: What do boxing and architecture have in common? For Tadao Ando, it’s a lot - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Tadao Ando Explores Parallels Between Architecture and Boxing in Memoir
articles.excerpt: Eighty-five-year-old architect Tadao Ando shares his life, boxing background, and design philosophy in his first English memoir, Towards Light.
articles.content: Eighty-five-year-old Japanese architect Tadao Ando has detailed the surprising parallels between his brief past as a professional boxer and his renowned architecture career. Having boxed briefly in Osaka during his youth, Ando notes that both disciplines demand a solitary stoic struggle to overcome personal fears and discover hidden strengths. Programmatic and budget constraints in architecture, much like the rigid demands of boxing, force a deep examination of what is truly necessary in design. Raised in working-class postwar Osaka, Ando taught himself architecture from books and completed his first major critical breakthrough, the Row House in Sumiyoshi, in 1976, later receiving the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1995. Translated by Polly Barton and published by Scribe Publications, his new memoir, Towards Light: A Philosophy of Life and Architecture, ventures far beyond technical architectural theory to chronicle personal anecdotes and the author's broader life philosophy. Rather than following a strict chronological structure, Ando wrote freely from his accumulated memories. The book is priced at 25 pounds and aims to leave readers with a renewed sense of hope and inspiration to pursue new paths.

articles.originalTitle: sandbag castle casts sustainable concrete alternatives into floating installation in eindhoven - Designboom
articles.title: Floating Installation in Eindhoven Showcases Low-Carbon Concrete Alternatives
articles.excerpt: Visual artist Yvonne Mak has brought together over ten low-carbon concrete alternatives in her floating installation Sandbag Castle, displayed on the Dommel river in Eindhoven, to address the environmental impact of conventional cement.
articles.content: Visual artist Yvonne Mak highlights the environmental impact of conventional cement with her floating installation Sandbag Castle, positioned in the Dommel river beside the Van Abbemuseum Café in Eindhoven. Measuring 5 meters wide and 3 meters high, the structure consists of hundreds of concrete modules resembling stacked sandbags. The design references temporary flood barriers and the widespread reliance on concrete for protective infrastructure. Red warning flags featuring a custom coat of arms with symbols for water, bridges, flora, and hands are positioned at the top of the structure. The physical composition of the work directly incorporates over 10 distinct low-carbon concrete variants, including calcined clay, alternative binders, geopolymer concrete, recycled aggregates, and self-healing concrete formulations. Developed with main partner TBI alongside specialized material and technology contributors, the work demonstrates existing and emerging structural alternatives designed to reduce CO₂ emissions in construction.

articles.originalTitle: David Chipperfield Architects builds concrete gallery around singular artwork in Germany - Dezeen
articles.title: David Chipperfield Architects Builds Concrete Gallery for Singular Artwork in Germany
articles.excerpt: David Chipperfield Architects has completed a monolithic concrete gallery on the grounds of Germany's Carmen Würth Forum to house a single large-scale painting by Anselm Kiefer.
articles.content: The Berlin office of David Chipperfield Architects has added a monolithic concrete gallery to the grounds of the Carmen Würth Forum museum in Künzelsau, Germany. The structure was built specifically to house Schwarze Flocken, an 11-by-7.1-meter artwork by German painter Anselm Kiefer that was previously too large to exhibit within the main museum. Named after a poem by Holocaust survivor Paul Celan, the Anselm Kiefer Pavilion features a cuboid shape constructed from brick and bush-hammered concrete, referencing the neighboring museum building completed in 2020. The form traces the interior volume specified by the artist. Inside, the walls are lined with clay plaster and the timber roof structure is left exposed. Rooflights let in natural light to create a tranquil atmosphere that shifts throughout the seasons. The three-layer wall construction, comprising concrete, brickwork, and internal clay plaster, adapts to varying climatic conditions without requiring active climate control parameters.

articles.originalTitle: Collected - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery to Exhibit Works Acquired for Public Care
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London is bringing together more than 40 works acquired for public care through the Acceptance in Lieu and Cultural Gifts schemes for the first time.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London will host a new exhibition titled Collected from 22 May to 5 September 2027, showcasing a unique selection of rare art works brought from private collections into public care across the UK. Held in the Ground Floor Galleries, the exhibition gathers more than 40 pieces for the first time, featuring paintings and ceramics by Picasso, a glittering cup with a millennium-old history, and an 18th-century goldfish bowl owned by an eccentric collector. Visitors will encounter works by Rembrandt, Renoir and Lucian Freud alongside rare objects acquired through the Art Council’s Acceptance in Lieu and Cultural Gifts schemes. Notable pieces include items accepted by the government in lieu of tax with additional grants from heritage funds. Standard admission operates on a pay-what-you-wish basis, while gallery members enjoy unlimited free entry to all paid exhibitions. The exhibition is supported by Adrian Sassoon and Edmund Burke, offering a comprehensive journey through centuries of artistic treasures and shared cultural heritage.

articles.originalTitle: Reenvisioning histories of American art: transforming museum practice - Rijksmuseum.nl
articles.title: Reenvisioning Histories of American Art: Transforming Museum Practice
articles.excerpt: As museums face mounting pressure to reckon with histories built on exclusion and exploitation, a new volume highlights scholarship and museum practices aimed at diversifying collections, exhibitions, and staffs.
articles.content: In recent years, museums have faced increasing pressure to reckon with their histories and legacies, many of which depended on exclusion, exploitation, and theft. This institutional self-reflection has emerged alongside a focus on incorporating antiracism and decolonization throughout museum work. Although more museums seek to diversify and make their collections, exhibitions, and staffs inclusive, very little has been published about the actual processes involved in this work. Published by Dartmouth's The Hood Museum of Art in association with the University of Washington Press, a new volume emerged from this ongoing dialogue. The publication highlights new scholarship and museum practices in diversifying collections, exhibitions, and staffs. It discusses new frameworks for how museums develop institutional priorities and aims to interrupt colonial structures in museum curation and teaching art history. Contributions cover topics ranging from collaborative methodologies and Native art acquisitions to Black feminist domesticity and Asian Americana. The volume is available for research use within the Rijksmuseum Research Library.

articles.originalTitle: Anatomy and Astronomy in the National Art Library - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: National Art Library Highlights Early Medical and Astronomical Textbooks
articles.excerpt: The National Art Library at the Victoria and Albert Museum houses rare early textbooks focusing on human anatomy and astronomy.
articles.content: The National Art Library within the Victoria and Albert Museum maintains rare early volumes on human anatomy and astronomy among its collections. Notable items include Andreas Vesalius's volume commonly known as De humani corporis fabrica libri septem, widely regarded as the first accurate anatomical textbook. Working during the Italian Renaissance, the Padua professor collaborated with German artist Jan Steven van Calcar to produce over 250 woodcut illustrations detailing internal human structures. Another scientific volume held in the library is the 1799 second edition of A compendious system of astronomy by Margaret Bryan, a school founder who compiled her lectures on planetary distances and motions for students. The publication refers to Uranus by the historical designation Georgium Sidus, a name utilized for decades following the planet's discovery. These volumes form part of the institution's Clements Collection and are accessible for viewing by appointment within the special collections reading rooms after standard registration.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the collectors | Laurent Dumas - Art Basel
articles.title: New Contemporary Art Center Le Large Opens in Boulogne-Billancourt
articles.excerpt: Emerige real estate group opens Le Large in Boulogne-Billancourt, launching its inaugural contemporary art exhibition titled Moteur Imaginaire.
articles.content: A new contemporary art center dedicated to showcasing excellence, Le Large, opens on the western edge of Greater Paris in Boulogne-Billancourt. Established by the real estate group Emerige, the center focuses particularly on artists living and working in France. For its inaugural exhibition, titled Moteur Imaginaire, the venue explores the history of Île Seguin, which served as a major manufacturing site for the French car manufacturer Renault until its closure in 1992. Italian curator Cecilia Alemani has brought together around 60 artists for the exhibition, including Neïl Beloufa, Bianca Bondi, Théo Mercier, Jean-Luc Moulène, and Laure Prouvost. The exhibition aims to present the carmaker's art collection, which is rarely exhibited in France, to a broader public, examining the evolution of machines and human interaction. The inaugural exhibition runs from 17 October 2026 to 7 March 2027. Additionally, Laurent Dumas will participate in related conversation events as part of seasonal cultural programmes.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026: performances, lectures, discussions, roundtables - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Announces Public Programme for Final Days of Art Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The final days of the 61st International Art Exhibition in Venice will feature public performances, lectures, and discussions at the Arsenale.
articles.content: The final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition in Venice will feature a public programme of performances, lectures, debates, and roundtables at the Arsenale spaces. Titled In Minor Keys and curated by Koyo Kouoh, the concluding phase of the exhibition will host an Assembly bringing together ten artist-led organisations and collectives to share creative practices, research, and ideas related to community and pedagogy. The schedule includes a series of performances, some created specifically for the occasion, by artists such as Laurie Anderson, Ziad Antar, rana elnemr, Natalia Lassalle-Morillo and Sofiá Gallisá Muriente, Clarissa Herbst, Tammy Nguyen, Hagar Ophir, Yo-E Ryou, Dominique Rust, Lerato Shadi, and Nathalie Vairac. Alongside the performances, speakers including Felwine Sarr will deliver lectures, while panel discussions will feature representatives from international cultural organisations discussing collaborative practices, resilience, and archival projects. The events will take place from Friday 13th to Sunday 22nd November.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.
